stem.en: A solid crystal of sodium chloride is placed in a circuit with a bulb. Why does the bulb stay dark?

text.en: Its ions are held in fixed places, so no charge can travel through the crystal.
The crystal has no charges at all until it is put in water.
Salt contains no electrons, so no current can pass.

explanation.en: The charges are there: the crystal is full of Na⁺ and Cl⁻. But each ion is held in place by the strong attraction of its neighbours, and a current needs charges that can travel. Option b forgets that the ions formed when the electron moved, long before any water. Option c is false, because Na⁺ and Cl⁻ both still have electrons.

hints.en: A current is moving charge. Ask two separate questions: are charges present, and can they travel?
